answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost. A voyage stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a violet holds...
